title: Instance
description: instance.yaml — the deployment-owned provisioning file `goobers init` writes first and the first file an operator edits. It declares which repositories this instance connects to, WHERE each credential is read from (never the value itself, CFG-009/SEC-010), and the instance-wide runner claims, run conditions, and telemetry every gaggle inherits. Gaggle/goober/workflow definitions are config-as-code reconciled from the workflow source; this file is provisioning, so it is loaded strictly — an unknown field is an error, never a silently ignored setting.

apiVersion.description: API version of this instance file.

repos.description: Repositories this instance connects to. Every gaggle's project and backlog must resolve to an entry here — a gaggle whose provider/owner/name matches no entry has no credential and can never run — so this list, not the gaggle, is where a repository's identity and auth live.

selfIdentity.description: Provider login this instance acts as, used for assignment-aware backlog selection. An identity value, never a credential. A gaggle's own spec.selfIdentity overrides it; empty leaves assignment-aware selection opted out.

needsHumanAssignee.description: Provider identity work items are assigned to when Goobers parks them for human attention. Empty leaves parked items unassigned, so nobody is notified.

credentials.description: Per-capability and per-MCP credential sources. A capability entry overrides the repo-token default for that one capability (e.g. a separate review identity, since an author cannot approve its own pull request); an MCP entry is reachable only through a goober's explicit MCP server reference. Agentic stages fall back to the current user's stored harness sign-in when no agent:model entry is configured, which is why a headless service account needs one.

daemonIdentity.description: Distinct bot identity for the daemon's own authored pull requests, reviews, merges, and comments (UNOP-7). Omitted keeps every mutation on the repository token. Configuring it backs the standard daemon-mutation capability set (repo:push, github:issues:write, github:pr:write, github:pr:review, github:branch:delete, github:pr:merge) without declaring each one under credentials; an explicit credentials entry for one of those still wins.

secretStores.description: Named external secret stores a token ref may resolve through (SEC-010). A store declares WHERE a secret lives, never a value; any token ref then opts in with `store: <storeName>/<secretName>` instead of env/file. Authentication to the store itself always uses an ambient identity — never a token ref, which would be circular. An instance that declares no stores and uses only env/file refs behaves exactly as it did before this field existed.

workflowSource.description: Where the definitions-as-code tree (gaggles, goobers, workflows) is read from, independently of the target code repositories. Omitted keeps the local <instance-root>/config directory.

runner.description: This runner's static claims and execution defaults: the toolchains it advertises, the extra ambient environment variables stages may see, and the baseline stage deadline.

engine.description: Tier-3 Temporal engine connection shared by the runtime, scheduler, workers, dispatchers, and daemon projection loop. GOOBERS_TEMPORAL_HOSTPORT, GOOBERS_TEMPORAL_NAMESPACE, and GOOBERS_TASK_QUEUE override these values at process startup.

runConditions.description: Instance-wide ceilings on top of each workflow's own readiness block. They only ever narrow what a workflow already permits.

telemetry.description: Local telemetry rollup store, optional collector push, and journal/rollup retention.

externalTelemetry.description: Named, read-only operational telemetry connectors workflows may query. A workflow selects only a connector name and generic query inputs, so provider-specific fields stay confined to this section.

connectors.description: Connector instances available to workflows, addressed by name. Names are unique within the instance.

retention.description: Opt-in pruning of retained failure worktrees and merged local run branches, plus the portal projection window. Distinct from telemetry.retention, which bounds journals and rollups.

notifications.description: Opts `goobers up` into native desktop notifications for escalated and failed runs. The one-shot daemon override is `goobers up --notify` (`--notify=all` adds completed and aborted runs).

speech.description: Opt-in local speech sink for the same terminal alerts. Omitted stays silent.

sandbox.description: Instance-wide isolation posture for agentic stages. Omitted (or `disabled`) runs agentic stages directly on the host, exactly as before it existed — isolation is strictly opt-in. A gaggle may STRENGTHEN this posture through its own spec.sandbox but never weaken an operator-enforced one.

agentic.description: Isolation posture for agentic stages. `enforced` requires the runner to isolate every agentic stage and FAILS runs it cannot isolate, so enable it only where the runner can actually sandbox.

workcopies.description: How managed mirrors and worktrees are provisioned. Omitted keeps every default; existing mirrors are never migrated in either direction when these change.

api.description: The daemon's read-only HTTP API (the portal's backend).

webhook.description: Optional provider webhook receiver. The daemon starts this listener only when a secret is configured AND at least one workflow declares a webhook trigger, so configuring it alone changes nothing.

listen.description: host:port for the webhook listener. Loopback hosts only — a non-loopback host is refused at load. Empty defaults to 127.0.0.1:8081.

secret.description: Where the provider webhook signing secret is read from. Exactly one source; never an inline value.

portal.description: Operator-supplied dashboard co-branding. Cosmetic only — nothing here affects scheduling or credentials.

timezone.description: IANA location name every workflow's cron schedule is evaluated in. Empty defaults to UTC — a fixed, reproducible zone rather than whatever the host process's local zone happens to be. An unresolvable name is rejected at load, not at the first tick.

tokenRef.description: Where a credential is READ FROM — never the value itself (CFG-009, SEC-010). Exactly one source per ref: an environment variable name, a file path, a macOS Keychain service name, or a secret in a declared secretStores entry. An inline secret value is rejected at load.

env.description: Name of an environment variable holding the token, read from the DAEMON process — so it must be exported before `goobers up`, not inside a stage. A name that stages can also see (through runner.envPassthrough or the built-in allowlist) is refused for secrets that must never reach a stage.

file.description: Path to a file whose entire contents are the token.

keychain.description: Service name of a generic-password item in the macOS login keychain.

store.description: Secret in a declared secret store, written as `<storeName>/<secretName>`. The store name must match a secretStores entry; the secret name is interpreted by that store's resolver.

repo.description: One target repository and the identity this instance reaches it with. GitHub and Gitea are two-part (owner/name); Azure DevOps is THREE-part (organization/project/repository) — owner carries the organization and project carries the middle segment.

provider.description: Backing system for this repository. It selects both the API surface and which auth kinds are accepted.

baseUrl.description: Forge root URL (e.g. https://gitea.example.com). Required for provider `gitea`, which has no fixed host; omitted for github and ado.

owner.description: GitHub organization or user, Gitea owner, or Azure DevOps ORGANIZATION (the first segment of dev.azure.com/<organization>).

project.description: Azure DevOps PROJECT — the middle segment of the three-part organization/project/repository identity. Required for provider `ado`; rejected for github and gitea, where it has no meaning.

name.description: Repository name — the last segment of the identity.

token.description: Where this repository's credential is read from. Required for PAT auth on every provider. It must be ABSENT for an auth kind that mints or borrows an identity (github-app, azure-cli, workload-identity, managed-identity): exactly one identity mechanism per repository, since a token alongside a minted one could only act as a silent fallback.

auth.description: Non-default credential source for this repository. Omitted means PAT auth with token configured — byte-identical to an instance that predates this block.

policy.description: This repository's declared forge-conformance manifest: the live settings `goobers doctor --repo` diffs against. GitHub-only. Omitted declares no expectation and changes nothing.

largeRepo.description: Enables the monolith-safe execution preset (pinned serial workspace, 4h stage timeout, path-length preflight, retention exemption, narrowed mirror refresh). The preset supplies DEFAULTS only — every explicit setting below overrides it.

workspace.description: How this repository is materialized for local runs. Pinned mode is deliberately non-hermetic: ignored and untracked build state may persist between runs, so the repository's .gitignore hygiene becomes load-bearing for clean run-branch diffs.

pathLength.description: Checkout path-length preflight for this repository. Declaring the block enables it on every host, not just Windows; set disabled to opt out.

defaultStageTimeout.description: Deadline for this repository's deterministic stages that declare no timeoutSeconds. It overrides both the large-repo preset and the instance-wide runner.defaultStageTimeout.

runControls.description: Watchdog budgets for runs targeting this repository, overriding runConditions. Gaggle and workflow runControls remain more specific.

repoAuth.description: Credential SOURCE selector for one repository — never credential material. Kind values are provider-specific: github accepts pat and github-app; ado accepts pat, azure-cli, workload-identity, and managed-identity; gitea accepts no auth block at all (static token only). Fields belonging to another provider's kinds are rejected at load rather than ignored.

kind.description: Identity mechanism: `pat` reads the static token ref; `github-app` mints short-lived installation tokens (GitHub); `azure-cli` borrows the current local az login, `workload-identity` uses federated Azure workload identity, and `managed-identity` uses an Azure managed identity (all Azure DevOps). Every kind except `pat` forbids a token ref on the same repository.

tenant.description: Pins Azure CLI authentication to one tenant. Azure DevOps only.

clientId.description: Selects a user-assigned managed identity. Valid only with kind `managed-identity`.

appId.description: GitHub App identifier for kind `github-app`: the numeric App ID or the App's client ID string — GitHub accepts either as the App JWT issuer.

installationId.description: Numeric ID of the App's installation on this repository's owner, for kind `github-app`. It must be the installation ID, not the App ID.

privateKey.description: Where the App's PEM-encoded private key is read from, for kind `github-app`. The key only ever signs short-lived App JWTs in this process; stages receive minted installation tokens, never the key, so an env name that stages can see is refused.

repoPolicy.description: Declared expectations about a repository's live branch protection, checked by `goobers doctor --repo`. Deployment-owned rules, which is why they live here rather than in workflow config. Nothing here changes the repository; it only reports drift.

branch.description: Branch these expectations apply to. Empty defaults to main.

requiredMergeMethod.description: The one merge method the repository must allow exclusively. Set it when a squash-only ruleset and a merge-commit setting can disagree; empty imposes no requirement.

mergeQueueRequired.description: Requires the branch to use the provider's native merge queue rather than accepting a direct-merge path.

requiredStatusChecks.description: Check contexts the branch's live rules must require. Entries are matched by exact context name, so a renamed CI job silently stops being required — that rename is what this list catches.

credentialGrant.description: One credential source for exactly one capability OR one named BYO MCP credential. Set exactly one of capability and mcp; each may be sourced only once per instance.

capability.description: Canonical capability this token backs, overriding the repository-token default for that capability alone. `agent:model` is the agent harness credential; github:pr:review needs a DIFFERENT identity from the one authoring pull requests, because an author cannot approve its own. Runner-owned capabilities are not grantable here — configrepo:read comes from workflowSource.token.

mcp.description: Name of a bring-your-own MCP credential. It is NOT a stage capability: it is reachable only by goobers whose MCP server declarations reference this name.

token.description: Where this credential is read from — exactly one source, never an inline value.

daemonIdentity.description: The identity the daemon authors its own provider mutations as. Omitted is byte-identical to an instance that never declared one.

kind.description: Identity mechanism: `pat` reads a machine account's token ref; `github-app` mints installation tokens. New mechanisms are additive kinds, never a change to these two.

token.description: Where the machine account's token is read from, for kind `pat`. Rejected for kind `github-app`, whose token is minted.

appId.description: GitHub App identifier for kind `github-app` (see repos[].auth.appId).

installationId.description: Numeric installation ID for kind `github-app` (see repos[].auth.installationId).

privateKey.description: Where the App's PEM-encoded private key is read from, for kind `github-app`.

slug.description: The App's URL-safe handle — the part before `[bot]` in its login. Installation tokens cannot self-report a login the way a token can, so pull-request attribution needs it declared explicitly.

secretStore.description: One named external secret store. Declaring a store no ref uses is harmless.

name.description: Handle store-backed token refs address this store by. A lowercase DNS label, so it can never be confused with the `/`-separated secret name that follows it in a ref.

kind.description: Store vendor. The seam is vendor-neutral by name+kind indirection; azure-key-vault is the only kind implemented today.

vaultURI.description: The https vault endpoint — scheme and host only, no path, query, fragment, or userinfo.

auth.description: How this process authenticates to the store. Always an ambient identity, never a token ref — a token ref would need a secret to read a secret.

kind.description: Ambient identity chain used to reach the store.

clientId.description: Pins a user-assigned identity. Valid for workload-identity and managed-identity; azure-cli has no client to pin.

cacheTTLSeconds.description: Bounds the in-memory cache of resolved secrets, so a value rotated in the vault is picked up within the TTL with no restart and without re-reading the store on every resolve. Zero or omitted keeps the resolver default of 300 seconds.

workflowSource.description: Location of the definitions-as-code tree. A local-dir source reads a directory directly; a git source reads a committed ref from either a local repository path or a remote https URL.

kind.description: How the workflow tree is obtained. `local-dir` accepts only path; `git` accepts exactly one of path or url.

path.description: Directory (kind local-dir) or local repository (kind git) holding the definitions tree.

url.description: Remote https git URL holding the definitions tree. Requires its own token ref.

ref.description: Committed git ref that is tracked. Empty defaults to main. Valid only for kind git.

token.description: Where the credential for a REMOTE git source is read from. This token reads the config repository, so it is deliberately not exposed to stages: an env name stages can also see is refused at load.

runner.description: What this runner advertises and how it bounds a stage. These are claims and defaults, not installation instructions: Goobers never installs a toolchain.

capabilities.description: Toolchain and platform capabilities this runner claims are ALREADY INSTALLED. The scheduler admits a run only when this set contains every capability the run's gaggle (spec.requiredCapabilities) and stages (task requiredCapabilities) declare, so a gaggle requiring `dotnet@8` on a runner that does not claim it never schedules a single run — the run does not fail, it never starts. Empty claims nothing, which is correct only while no gaggle or stage requires anything. Matching is exact string membership, so `dotnet@8` and `dotnet@10` are distinct capabilities, never a range. A false claim is not caught here: it degrades to a runtime error in the stage that needs the toolchain.

envPassthrough.description: Additional ambient environment variable NAMES carried from the daemon process into every deterministic stage and harness subprocess, on top of the built-in default-deny allowlist. That allowlist already covers PATH/HOME/TMPDIR, Windows profile and shell paths, locale and proxy variables, and the Go, .NET/NuGet, Python, Node, Rust, and Java/Maven/Gradle toolchain families — so this list is for a variable those families miss, such as a private NUGET_CONFIG_FILE or a bespoke FOO_HOME. It stays default-deny: an explicit opt-in list of names, never a value and never a whole-environment passthrough. A name whose variable is unset is a harmless no-op, and a name that would expose a configured secret ref to stages is refused at load.

items.description: A POSIX-shaped environment variable name. Malformed names are rejected at load rather than mis-split at stage launch.

defaultStageTimeout.description: Baseline deadline for a deterministic stage that declares no timeoutSeconds of its own, as a Go duration. Unset keeps the built-in 10 minutes, which is sized for short commands rather than a mature repository's build+test entrypoint: if `make ci` routinely runs 15 minutes, raise this once here instead of stamping timeoutSeconds onto every such stage in every workflow. A stage's own timeoutSeconds always wins; this only moves the floor. Sizing it too low is not free — a timed-out stage is reported retryable, so a workflow that routes the failure to an agent spends a repass on something no diff can fix.

livenessTimeout.description: Maximum age of the scheduler tick heartbeat before the daemon reports itself unhealthy. Empty defaults to 2 minutes; values below 2 seconds are rejected.

harnessCommand.description: Overrides the base CLI invocation (argv[0..]) launched for a harness, keyed by harness name. Unset keys keep the built-in default. This is the adopter escape hatch for running the same engine CLI through a wrapper — the wrapper name lives only in this file, never in the harness enum. It replaces the launch prefix only, so it is safe solely for a launcher that honors the same CLI contract (session capture, completion-file readback) as the harness it overrides.

additionalProperties.description: Full argv for the harness launcher. The first element is the program and must be non-empty.

engine.description: Temporal frontend and routing configuration. Omitted fields use the documented local defaults.

hostPort.description: Temporal frontend in host:port form. GOOBERS_TEMPORAL_HOSTPORT overrides this value.

namespace.description: Temporal namespace. Defaults to `default`; GOOBERS_TEMPORAL_NAMESPACE overrides this value.

taskQueue.description: Task queue used for engine workflows and activities. Defaults to `goobers-engine`; GOOBERS_TASK_QUEUE overrides this value.

runnerCapability.description: A free-form, version-parameterized runner capability token (e.g. dotnet@8, xcode, os=windows) — distinct from a credential capability, and deliberately not a closed enum. An alphanumeric start then letters, digits, and any of . _ - + @ =, no whitespace.

harnessName.description: An agent harness whose launcher may be overridden.

githubId.description: A GitHub identifier that may be written as a number (appId: 123456) or a quoted string; both parse to the same value.

duration.description: A Go duration string such as 30s, 45m, or 6h. Must be positive.

runConditions.description: Instance-level ceilings. They sit on top of, and never widen, each workflow's own readiness guardrails.

maxParallelRuns.description: Total concurrent runs allowed across every workflow in this instance. Zero or omitted leaves concurrency bounded only by each workflow's own limits, which on a laptop-class host is usually not what you want — `goobers init` writes 1.

workflowBudgets.description: Per-workflow runs-per-HOUR ceiling, keyed by workflow name. An entry REPLACES that workflow's own maxRunsPerHour rather than combining with it. A name matching no workflow is inert.

additionalProperties.description: Maximum runs per hour for the named workflow. Zero stops it from starting.

workflowDailyBudgets.description: Per-workflow runs-per-DAY ceiling, keyed by workflow name — the daily twin of workflowBudgets, applied in addition to it.

additionalProperties.description: Maximum runs per day for the named workflow. Zero stops it from starting.

maxRepasses.description: Instance default for how many times gates may cumulatively route a run back to the same already-completed stage before escalation, regardless of gate or outcome. Omitted uses the built-in default; a gaggle, repository, or workflow runControls value is more specific.

stalledRunTimeout.description: How long a running journal may stay silent before the watchdog escalates the run. Empty defaults to 45 minutes. Size it above your slowest single stage, or a healthy long stage looks stalled.

maxRunDuration.description: Maximum total wall-clock age of a run. Empty disables the limit.

claimsLockTimeout.description: Bounds cross-process claim-ledger lock acquisition, so a wedged holder cannot convoy stage dispatch or terminal cleanup. Empty defaults to 30 seconds.

telemetry.description: Local rollup store, optional collector push, and journal retention.

enabled.description: Toggles span emission, local SQLite ingest, and any configured collector push. Disabling it also forbids an OTLP endpoint, since there would be nothing to push.

otlp.description: Optional OTLP/gRPC collector push. Absent (and no GOOBERS_OTLP_ENDPOINT in the environment) means no push at all — local rollups are unaffected.

endpoint.description: Collector endpoint. The GOOBERS_OTLP_ENDPOINT environment variable overrides this value at load.

insecure.description: Sends to the collector without TLS. Acceptable for a loopback collector; GOOBERS_OTLP_INSECURE overrides it.

headers.description: Extra gRPC headers, keyed by header name. Every value is an indirect secret ref, never a literal header value.

retention.description: Bounds terminal run journals and their rollup rows. Automatic pruning is OPT-IN: with this block absent nothing is ever pruned, and `goobers telemetry prune --dry-run` can preview the same policy at any time.

enabled.description: Lets the daemon prune automatically. False keeps the policy available to explicit prune commands only.

window.description: Age beyond which terminal runs are prunable, as a Go duration or a whole number of days (90d). Empty uses 90 days.

maxRuns.description: Maximum terminal runs retained regardless of age. Zero or omitted uses 500.

externalTelemetryConnector.description: One named, read-only telemetry connector instance. Workflows reference it by name only.

name.description: Handle workflows select this connector by. Unique within the instance.

kind.description: Registered connector kind that builds this instance.

version.description: Connector contract version this configuration was written against.

config.description: Connector-kind-specific settings, validated by that kind's factory. Required — a connector with no config cannot be built.

auth.description: How this connector acquires its credential. Omitted means no credential (mode `none`).

mode.description: Credential acquisition mode. `bearer-token` requires exactly one of token.env or token.file; every other mode forbids a token ref.

token.description: Where the bearer token is read from — exactly one of env or file, never an inline value. An env name that stages can also see is refused at load.

env.description: Name of an environment variable holding the token.

file.description: Path to a file whose contents are the token.

tenant.description: Pins Azure authentication to one tenant.

policy.description: Host-side ceilings for this connector. They bound what a workflow query may consume; a connector can never raise them.

timeout.description: Maximum wall-clock time for one query.

maxAttempts.description: Total attempts including the first; one disables retries.

maxRows.description: Maximum rows returned before the result is marked truncated.

maxBytes.description: Maximum result size in bytes before the result is marked truncated.

network.description: The ONLY network access this connector's host-provided HTTP client allows. An empty allowlist permits nothing.

allowedHosts.description: Hosts this connector may reach. Anything else is refused by the host HTTP boundary, not by the connector.

allowHTTP.description: Permits plaintext http:// to the allowed hosts. Off keeps every request https.

retention.description: Opt-in cleanup of on-disk run remains and the portal's listable history window.

enabled.description: Enables pruning of retained terminal-failure worktrees and merged local run branches. It requires at least one of maxRetainedWorktreeBytes or retainedWorktreeMaxAge — enabling retention with no limits would prune nothing. Active runs are never candidates.

dryRun.description: Reports the deterministic candidate set without deleting anything.

maxRetainedWorktreeBytes.description: Byte ceiling for retained failure worktrees; the oldest are removed first once exceeded. Zero or omitted disables the size rule.

retainedWorktreeMaxAge.description: Age beyond which a retained failure worktree is prunable. Empty disables the age rule.

projectionFullFidelityDays.description: How many days of history stay INDIVIDUALLY LISTABLE in the portal. Independent of journal retention: the journal is the source of truth, this is only about what the derived projection lists, so aging a run out removes no evidence. Zero, unset, or negative means UNBOUNDED — never a zero-day window.

speech.description: Local speech sink for terminal alerts. Enabled explicitly; the engine must exist on the host.

enabled.description: Speaks the same alerts the terminal prints.

engine.description: Speech backend. `auto` selects whichever of say/espeak the host provides.

voice.description: Engine-specific voice name. It must not begin with `-` or contain control characters.

language.description: BCP 47-style language tag such as en-US.

rate.description: Speaking rate in words per minute, within the engine's supported range.

timeout.description: Maximum time one utterance may take before it is abandoned.

workcopies.description: Managed mirror and worktree provisioning. Each option applies to NEWLY created mirrors only — existing mirrors are never migrated either way.

root.description: Absolute base path for managed mirrors and worktrees. The gaggle name and repository key are appended beneath it, preserving workforce isolation. A gaggle's own workcopies.root overrides it.

partialClone.description: Provisions new mirrors as blobless partial clones with a heads+tags refresh refspec — the large-repo clone-time and disk win. Blobs are then fetched on demand when a stage worktree materializes, so worktree creation becomes network-dependent (and, on private repositories, credential-dependent). Off keeps full mirrors with byte-identical git behavior.

objectCache.description: Lets new mirrors borrow objects from a shared node-level object cache via git alternates: one bare clone per repository URL shared by every gaggle on the node, instead of one full clone per gaggle. Off never creates the cache directory.

api.description: The daemon's read-only HTTP API. The default posture is tier-1 local trust: loopback only, no authenticator.

listen.description: host:port for the API listener. Empty defaults to 127.0.0.1:8080. A NON-loopback host is refused at load unless BOTH tls and auth are configured — fail closed, with no insecure override.

tls.description: Serves the API over HTTPS from an on-disk certificate and key. Required for a non-loopback listen address.

certFile.description: Path to the PEM certificate. A path only — key material never appears in this file.

keyFile.description: Path to the PEM private key. A path only.

auth.description: Replaces the tier-1 null authenticator. Required for a non-loopback listen address.

oidc.description: Validates bearer JWTs against one issuer and maps its claims onto instance roles. Entra ID is a configured issuer here, not a separate code path.

issuer.description: Issuer URL exactly as tokens state it in `iss`. Discovery uses <issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration.

audience.description: The `aud` claim value tokens must carry.

rolesClaim.description: Claim carrying role or group values. Empty defaults to `roles`.

roles.description: Maps claim values onto instance roles. DENY BY DEFAULT: an authenticated principal whose claim values match nothing gets no role at all. Roles nest — admin implies operate, operate implies view.

operate.description: Claim values granted run operations in addition to view.

admin.description: Claim values granted full control in addition to operate.

portal.description: Dashboard co-branding. Every field is optional and cosmetic.

brand.description: Instance identity shown in the portal header.

tagline.description: Short subtitle under the name. Empty defaults to `local operations`.

scopeMark.description: Short mark used where the full name does not fit. Empty derives the first letter of the name.

logoUrl.description: Logo path. It must start with /assets/ — the portal serves operator assets from that root and refuses off-instance URLs.

faviconUrl.description: Favicon path. It must start with /assets/.

theme.description: Accent color overrides. Each value must be a plausible CSS color; light and dark variants are set independently so neither theme is left unreadable.

accentLight.description: Primary accent in the light theme.

accentDark.description: Primary accent in the dark theme.

accentSoftLight.description: Muted accent fill in the light theme.

accentSoftDark.description: Muted accent fill in the dark theme.

accentInkLight.description: Text color drawn on the light accent.

accentInkDark.description: Text color drawn on the dark accent.

support.description: Support channels rendered in the portal sidebar.

docsUrl.description: Documentation link. It must start with https://.

issuesUrl.description: Issue tracker link. It must start with https://.

chatUrl.description: Chat link. It must start with https://, slack://, or msteams://.

links.description: Extra labeled links, at most six.

url.description: Link target. It must start with https://.
